claims.text: Under GRUDGE the project was reduced to a token effort until Ruppelt was placed in charge in late 1951.

edges.label: Ruppelt is the origin of public knowledge of the Estimate
edges.note: As a serving Blue Book director with access to the files, Ruppelt published the Estimate's existence and destruction in 1956; the Condon Report corroborated him twelve years later.

edges.label: Ruppelt was Blue Book's first director
edges.note: Ruppelt directed the project from March 1952 to August 1953, covering the Washington flap and the Robertson Panel, and later published the only insider account of the period.

edges.label: Ruppelt attended the panel as Blue Book director and later described it
edges.note: Ruppelt was present at the January 1953 sessions in his official capacity and published his account of the panel's function three years later.

edges.label: Vandenberg rejected the Estimate and ordered copies destroyed
edges.note: The Air Force Chief of Staff rejected the interplanetary conclusion for lacking proof and had the document destroyed — the earliest documented destruction of an adverse UAP record, attested in the Air Force's own contracted study.
